Thanks Claire / Kimberly — copied initial thoughts so Sales & Security have direction: 

1) Liability cap — commercial best practice is to offer a default cap at 12 months' fees (we can propose 12 months) but keep higher caps for deliberate security failures; we should preserve carve-outs for gross negligence and willful misconduct. If procurement pushes for higher, propose a stagger: 12 months standard, up to 24 months for enterprise pricing (requires exec approval).

2) Data residency — propose an Exhibit B (Data Residency & Hosting) that specifies region-by-region storage and processing. For EU-only requirement, offer Dedicated/EU-hosted option (Private or Dedicated) listed in Order Form as a deployable SKU; for hosted plan we can commit to EU-only backups and KV cache residency with audit logging retention controls. Jonas, can you confirm feasibility and any lead times for Dedicated EU pools?

3) Security evidence — we can provide SOC 2 Type II report (redacted) and the Redwood_Security_Summary.pdf. Recommend we include a 30-day SLA for initial security review responses and a 10-business-day turnaround for technical integration security calls.

Attaching: Redwood_Security_Summary.pdf

If Datasphere's procurement target is 2026-05-10, we should aim to finalize commercial terms by 2026-04-26 to allow legal review. Kimberly/Marissa — can Sales commit to that timeline?

— Rishi
